title: Walsingham letter-book, Feb 1572/3: Burghley to Walsingham, port name read as St Valery, BL Harley MS 260 f. 419 (DECODE R8364)

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 260 f. 419r-v; DECODE R8364

plaintext.source: Letter printed in Digges, The Compleat Ambassador (1655) p. 327 with the cipher left as signs; no decipherment found.

transcription.notes: 26 tokens: boxed [9] x5, 3 x4, tt, II, a 6-sign letter run (the port) and a 9-sign run. The earlier pass counted the port as 7 signs; the 7th (tt, Digges ℵ) is a separate person code. Digges 1655 p. 327 is a second witness.

system.summary: Burghley-Walsingham 1571-73 cipher: homophonic alphabet of digits, letters and signs, plus name codes and cover-names marked by a boxed digit; inserted in a clear letter.
system.notes: Key: TNA SP 106/2 f. 141A 'Sir Francis Walsingham Cipher, 1571' (Tu 2012), not on DECODE, not consulted. Same system in Harley 260 R8356-R8363 and about 45 passages printed by Digges 1655 (digges_corpus.tsv).

prior_solution.where: Digges 1655 p. 327 prints the letter with the cipher undeciphered; no decipherment found in print or on DECODE

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the two R8364 images with the DECODE cookie (decrypt-custom filesrv).
Identified f. 419 as Walsingham's letter-book; the cipher letter as Burghley to Walsingham, Feb 1572/3.
Found the letter printed in Digges 1655 p. 327, cipher undeciphered.
Transcribed the cipher tokens from the scans (26 tokens).
Place-name cribs for the 7-sign run, pooled with the R8361 run's shared signs; no unique alphabet.
CSP Foreign x, Feb 1573 (BHO pp. 243-271): letter not calendared, no decipherment.
Reopened: Digges p. 245 (Walsingham to Smith, Sept 1572) prints ~90 cipher signs, so the letter-book's cipher corpus is far larger than the earlier 25-sign count.
Located every cipher passage in Digges 1655 by hOCR word confidence and two page-by-page subagent scans of all 457 images; ~45 passages cropped and listed (digges_corpus.tsv).
CSP Foreign ix-x searched for letters 'partly in cipher, deciphered' to pair with Digges; no. 527 (10 Aug 1572) is deciphered but Digges omits its cipher sentence.
Tu 2012 thesis gives the key's shelfmark, TNA SP 106/2 f. 141A (Walsingham cipher 1571), and Cotton Vespasian F VI originals; neither online (DECODE lacks f. 141A; Vespasian F VI not digitised).
Viewed DECODE SP 106/2 keys R341-R354; R343 (f. 50, Norris-period, with Deepe/Calles/Dover) and R341 do not give sense or VALERY.

Aligned the port group across five copies in four letters (Digges pp. 301, 303, 313, 327; Harley R8363, R8364): six signs, constant 1st and 3rd; with the Vespasian F VI catalogue entry for a ship kept waiting at St Valery (Dec 1572), read VALERY.
Retried the nine-sign run with the partial alphabet (H = E) and cribs (passport, safe conduct, the Queene, Lord Seton, the Regent).

Person codes around the port re-examined for the quotation list (30 Sept): tt (subject of 'imagined') supplied as [they] and the lone 3 in 'if 3 should so do' as [Glasgow], both by sense only (grade I); no key, no second occurrence; nine-sign run still unread.

Adam Wright (email, 1 Oct 2026) pointed to the Folger Elizabethan Court Day by Day 1573, which summarises this letter under 29 Jan 1573 (after Read 1960, pp. 94-95). Aligned with our transcription: Davison = Maisonfleur, Hall = the Queen, Glasgow = Alencon (not James Beaton), [9] and tt = Alencon, the last gentleman = La Mole; 3 unresolved.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 12 tokens, 8 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.386 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcription.txt / cipher_tokens.txt (the cipher items in context) and reading.txt (the letter with the readings and the unread items marked)

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026). The cipher items in < > of reading.txt were taken one by one. Cover-name markers after a name in clear ([9] after Glascoe twice; 3 after Glascoe and Hall) carry no cipher and were left out. The 8 cipher words: VALERY read (grade M); [9] alone x3, tt and the lone 3, inferred as Alençon from the Folger/Read summary (grade I, not sure words); the nine-sign run (extent unknown, one word) and II unread. 1/8 = 0.125 (5/8 = 0.625 if the grade-I identifications counted). Was 0.977 over the whole letter, clear text included. The letter goes from read to read in part; the class was already read in part, and the token figure (6 of 26, 0.23) is unchanged.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.386; polyphony 0.0; 14 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached n/a

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The six-sign place name was read as (St) Valery by aligning five copies of the same homophonic group in four letters (Digges 1655 and Harley 260) with the BL catalogue entry for Cotton Vespasian F VI item 111, a French letter asking for a ship to wait at St Valery.
outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher_tokens.txt, cipher tokens: the 6-sign port read of 26 tokens
outcome.notes: Port read as (St) Valery, grade M. Nine-sign run, name codes 3, II, tt and the cover-name markers unread; key SP 106/2 f. 141A and the Cotton Vespasian F VI original not reachable. Verified by the same word in five copies across four letters and by the St Valery ship in the Vespasian F VI catalogue. 1 Oct 2026: names identified by sense from a Folger summary (Davison = Maisonfleur, Hall = the Queen, Glasgow = Alencon, [9] = Alencon, last gentleman = La Mole), grade I, not counted in fraction_read; Glasgow is not the Archbishop.

texts.label: Harley MS 260 f. 419r-v, 29 Jan 1573
texts.summary: Walsingham's letter-book copy of Burghley's letter of 29 Jan 1573 to Walsingham, ambassador in France, about Alençon's agents (Maisonfleur as 'Davison', La Mole as 'the laste gentleman') and the ship sent to (St) Valery. The six-sign place name is read as VALERY; the boxed [9] as Alençon from the Folger/Conyers Read summary (via Adam Wright); the nine-sign run and the name codes 3, tt and II stay unread.
texts.note: 16 Nov 2026: read share over cipher words only 0.125. The cipher words are the items in < > of reading.txt (cipher_tokens.txt), minus the boxed [9] and the 3 where they follow a cover-name in clear (Glascoe [9] twice, Glascoe 3, Hall 3 twice), markers that carry no cipher. That leaves 8: the six-sign port, read VALERY (grade M, counted read as in fraction_read); [9] standing alone three times, tt and the lone 3, identified with Alençon from the Folger/Conyers Read summary (grade I, inferred from the clear sense, so not sure words, as in fraction_read); the nine-sign run (extent unknown, counted as one word) and II, unread. 1 read of 8. With the grade-I identifications counted it would be 5 of 8 (0.625). Under the 95% bar, so read in part. Whole letter, clear included, not the measure: the 0.977 recorded before.
